rule: Every entry is an assumption, not a measurement. Geometry built from an entry must carry its id and be colour-coded as hypothesis in renders.

hypotheses.statement: One scan source unit is one millimetre.
hypotheses.basis: Declared by the project owner on 2026-11-06. Consistent with the fitted bore (22.62 mm) and a tip diameter of about 271 mm, but neither is an independent calibration.
hypotheses.clears_when: two independently measured dimensions of the same specimen agree through check_scan_calibration.py

hypotheses.statement: The back acquisition pass is treated as rigidly registered to the front for version 1.
hypotheses.basis: Measured offset of back faces: 0.27-0.69 degree tilt, 0.44 mm drum-centre shift (params/frame.json). The scan file name says the back was not lined up with the centre.
affects: back-facing surfaces: flange back face, lugs, lower bowl, blade pressure sides
hypotheses.clears_when: a separate rigid fit of the back faces is applied and the scorecard of back-facing regions improves

hypotheses.statement: The volume enclosed by the inner cone, the rolled lip and the outer drum/bowl is unobserved; version 1 revolves the observed outer loop as a closed section.
hypotheses.basis: The scanner sees only the outside of this section. The rolled lip is about 2.7 mm across, which suggests a formed or spun wall rather than a solid casting, but the wall thickness is not observed.
hypotheses.does_not_affect: aerodynamic surfaces, which are all observed
hypotheses.clears_when: a section, a photograph of a cut or damaged hub, or a measured mass of the specimen

hypotheses.statement: The front flange face carrying the bolt circle is used as datum A.
hypotheses.basis: Flattest large face of the hub (0.10 mm RMS). Its role as the mounting face to the drive output is not established.
hypotheses.clears_when: the drive output flange is identified on the drive scan or from a document
